comparison: Perfect agreement on methodology (C2, C29, C30, C31). Both evaluations recognize the high-pressure freezing combined with optogenetic stimulation as a validated and groundbreaking technical achievement. OpenEval notes 'well-validated methodological approach' while peer reviewers call it a 'tour de force' and 'remarkable.'

Strong agreement on exocytosis observations (C32-C35, C38-C40). Both accept the documentation of omega figures, docked/tethered vesicle depletion, and spatial distribution. OpenEval emphasizes statistical analysis while peer reviewers describe findings as 'lovely and comprehensive' and 'elegant.'

Agreement on spatial distribution of fusion events (C3, C36, C37, C41, C42, C68, C73). Both accept that fusion occurs throughout the active zone extending ~400nm radially. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm the broad active zone conclusion without challenge.

Strong agreement on correlation between morphological and electrophysiological recovery (C4, C43-C46, C50, C78, C80). Both evaluations validate that docked vesicle recovery matches paired-pulse depression recovery, supporting the RRP interpretation. Peer reviewer states this 'argues strongly' for tracking the correct physiological process.

Perfect agreement on adherens junction endocytosis (C6, C57, C58, C64, C71). Both accept the spatial localization and temporal dynamics at adherens junctions. OpenEval notes 'clearly documented' evidence while peer reviewers see 'no flaws in the experiments or interpretations.'

Agreement on rapid endocytosis temporal dynamics (C5, C51, C53-C55, C63, C70). Both accept the ultrafast timescale and size measurements. OpenEval notes 'well-documented through time-course analysis' while peer reviewers describe findings as 'elegant' with 'convincing' interpretations, though note the speed was unexpected.

Agreement on dynamin requirement (C59-C61, C88). Both accept that dynamin is necessary for endocytic vesicle resolution based on temperature-sensitive mutant experiments. Peer reviewer expresses disappointment with analysis depth but does not challenge the conclusion.

Divergence on interpretation challenging existing models (C7, C8, C62, C72). OpenEval expresses caution about claims inconsistent with existing models, noting membrane balance assumptions and incomplete exclusion of alternatives. Peer reviewers accept the challenge to existing models, stating 'I see no flaws in the experiments or interpretations' despite acknowledging results 'will be difficult to accept for some.'

Divergence on membrane balance calculations (C94-C98). OpenEval expresses uncertainty about multiple assumptions that may introduce systematic errors. Peer reviewers explicitly validate this analysis, stating 'The fact that the analysis of the amount of exo matches the analysis for the amount of endo strongly suggests that the authors are tracking the right stuff here.'

Agreement on uncertainty regarding speculation (C89, C90). Both evaluations express caution about why ultrafast endocytosis wasn't observed previously. OpenEval notes these are 'hypotheses for future testing rather than supported conclusions.' Peer reviewer questions whether optogenetic stimulus truly mimics physiological conditions, calling this 'the only real weakness.'

Agreement on selective depletion of docked vesicles (C74, C75, C83). Both accept that docked vesicles are preferentially consumed during stimulation. OpenEval notes 'clearly established with appropriate quantification' while peer reviewers accept the finding without challenge.

Agreement on size heterogeneity of endocytic structures (C86, C87). Both accept that invaginations are larger than synaptic vesicles. OpenEval provides explicit size measurements while peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall endorsement of endocytic findings.

Agreement on technical capability to preserve protein structures (C56, C93). Both accept that high-pressure freezing can preserve clathrin coats if present. Peer reviewer's question about dynamin immunogold implicitly accepts the preservation capability.

Divergence on spatial segregation interpretation (C69, C85). OpenEval groups this with uncertain claims about mechanism inconsistency. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the spatial organization, stating endocytic events occur in two zones while fusion occurs throughout the active zone.

Divergence on two-mechanism interpretation (C6, C64, C71 overlap). OpenEval supports the adherens junction endocytosis observations. Peer reviewer R15 challenges whether spatial differences represent two distinct mechanisms versus one mechanism with different time courses, requesting title modification.

Divergence on endocytic structure identity (C51, C53, C69-C71). OpenEval supports the endocytic interpretation based on temporal dynamics and controls. Peer reviewer R14 requests 'further evidence that the invaginations seen post-stimulation really do represent endocytic rather than exocytic structures,' suggesting additional confirmation needed.

OpenEval specifically evaluates vesicle accounting observations (C47, C48) as directly measured and internally consistent. No corresponding peer review result explicitly addresses these specific morphometric measurements in isolation.

Additional overlap on priming and refilling distinction (C44, C76-C78, C81-C82). OpenEval notes this is 'reasonably inferred from the data' with convergent evidence. Peer reviewers accept the correlation between recovery kinetics and vesicle replenishment, validating the physiological interpretation.
